RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone tells you almost nothing. In clinical laboratory medicine women are the majority of the workforce, so an all-female panel of four is unremarkable statistically. Raising it would read as insinuation without evidence and would cost you credibility — including for the legitimate complaint you do have.

The real issue is the unanswered request. Many jurisdictions give rejected applicants a right to written reasons, especially in public hospitals. Send a dated follow-up, in writing, to HR and the panel chair, citing the applicable rule.

Note too that senior-management posts routinely weight management track record over research depth. A PhD doesn't automatically outrank documented leadership experience. Get the reasons first, then judge.
